parole.significato: An alleged German idiom that portray Swedes as gullible or naive.
parole.testo: Pseudo-Germanism, derived from die (“the”) + dummen (“dumb, stupid”) + Schweden (“Swedes”). Debated origin: * Possibly from the Thirty Years' War (1618–1648) when Swedish soldiers from the countryside were accommodated in German cities, and were there easy targets for local tricksters, fraudsters an
Borrowed from German Heiduck, from Hungarian hajdúk. Cognate of English hajduk, Russian гайдук (gajduk).
Borrowed from German Kutscher, from Kutsche, from Hungarian kocsi, arguably from the name of the village Kocs. Doublet of coach. Cognate of English coach, French coche, Dutch koetsier.
From German Paprika, from Hungarian paprika, from Serbo-Croatian paprika.

parole.significato: sabre (a light sword, sharp along the front edge, part of the back edge, and at the point)
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Säbel (Late Middle High German sabel), from Hungarian szablya.
